description: A family retreat on a remote, heavily wooded coastal site on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast — conceived as a group of contemporary buildings stepping down to the shore. Heavy timber and local stone carry floor-to-ceiling glazing, so that at dusk the main pavilion reads as a lantern against the forest.

Every principal room holds the sea view. The master bath opens through two sets of bifolding doors to a private elevated terrace, its freestanding sculptural tub set against the water — a room featured internationally by Trends. Board-formed concrete stairs, a gallery over the lap pool, and glass balustrades cantilevered above the rocky foreshore carry the palette of raw concrete, bluestone and white oak through the whole house.
note: Named among the firm's award-winning projects in its own materials. Gallery recovered from the studio's original website via the Internet Archive.
